question.text: Consider the following system of linear equations: \[ \begin{cases} x -2y + z = 1 \\ 2x -y -z = -1 \\ -2x + 4y -2z = -2 \end{cases} \] Use the standard Gauss-Jordan method to reduce the augmented matrix $M$ of the system to reduced row echelon form.
question.explanation:
The augmented matrix for this system is \[ M= \left[ \begin{array}{ccc|c} 1 & -2 & 1 & 1 \\ 2 & -1 & -1 & -1 \\ -2 & 4 & -2 & -2 \\ \end{array} \right]. \]

Transforming $M$ to reduced row echelon form, we have

\[\begin{align*} M&\sim \left[\begin{array}{ccc|c} 1 & -2 & 1 & 1 \\ 2 & -1 & -1 & -1 \\ -2 & 4 & -2 & -2 \\ \end{array}\right] & R_2 &:= R_2 - 2R_1 \\[5pt] &\sim \left[\begin{array}{ccc|c} 1 & -2 & 1 & 1 \\ 0 & 3 & -3 & -3 \\ -2 & 4 & -2 & -2 \\ \end{array}\right]& R_3 &:= R_3 + 2R_1 \\[5pt] &\sim \left[\begin{array}{ccc|c} 1 & -2 & 1 & 1 \\ 0 & 3 & -3 & -3 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0 \\ \end{array}\right] & R_2 &:= \dfrac{1}{3}R_2 \\[5pt] &\sim \left[\begin{array}{ccc|c} 1 & -2 & 1 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & -1 & -1 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0 \\ \end{array}\right]. \end{align*}\]

In the row echelon form above, we have only two pivots (in the $1$st and $2$nd columns). To transform the matrix to reduced row echelon form, we need to create zeros above the pivots only. This gives,

\[\begin{align*} M&\sim \left[\begin{array}{ccc|c} 1 & -2 & 1 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & -1 & -1 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0 \\ \end{array}\right] & R_1 &:= R_1 + 2R_2 \\[5pt] &\sim \left[\begin{array}{ccc|c} 1 & 0 & -1 & -1 \\ 0 & 1 & -1 & -1 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0 \\ \end{array}\right]. \end{align*}\]

question.text: Consider the following system of linear equations: \[ \begin{cases} -x -y - 3z = 1 \\ 2x +2y + 6z = -2 \\ -2x - 2y - 6z = 2 \end{cases} \] Use the standard Gauss-Jordan method to reduce the augmented matrix $M$ of the system to reduced row echelon form.
question.explanation:
The augmented matrix for this system is \[ M= \left[ \begin{array}{ccc|c} -1 & -1 & -3 & 1 \\ 2 & 2 & 6 & -2 \\ -2 & -2 & -6 & 2 \\ \end{array} \right]. \]

Transforming $M$ to reduced row echelon form, we have

\[\begin{align*} M&\sim \left[\begin{array}{ccc|c} -1 & -1 & -3 & 1 \\ 2 & 2 & 6 & -2 \\ -2 & -2 & -6 & 2 \\ \end{array}\right] & R_1 &:=-R_1 \\[5pt] &\sim \left[\begin{array}{ccc|c} 1 & 1 & 3 & -1 \\ 2 & 2 & 6 & -2 \\ -2 & -2 & -6 & 2 \\ \end{array}\right]& R_2 &:= R_2 - 2R_1 \\[5pt] &\sim \left[\begin{array}{ccc|c} 1 & 1 & 3 & -1 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0 \\ -2 & -2 & -6 & 2 \\ \end{array}\right] & R_3 &:= R_3 + 2R_1 \\[5pt] &\sim \left[\begin{array}{ccc|c} 1 & 1 & 3 & -1 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0 \\ \end{array}\right]. \end{align*}\]

question.text: Consider the following system of linear equations: \[ \left\{ \begin{align*} &x - 3y =1\\ &y + 2z= 1\\ &5x-7y+17z =7 \\ \end{align*} \right. \] Use the standard Gauss-Jordan method to reduce the augmented matrix $M$ of the system to reduced row echelon form.
question.explanation:
The augmented matrix for this system is \[ M= \left[ \begin{array}{ccc|c} 1 & -3 & 0 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & 2 & 1 \\ 5 & -7 & 17 & 7 \\ \end{array} \right]. \]

Transforming $M$ to reduced row echelon form, we have

\[\begin{align*} M&\sim \left[\begin{array}{ccc|c} 1 & -3 & 0 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & 2 & 1 \\ 5 & -7 & 17 & 7 \\ \end{array}\right] & R_3&:= R_3 + (-5)R_1 \\[5pt] &\sim \left[\begin{array}{ccc|c} 1 & -3 & 0 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & 2 & 1 \\ 0 & 8 & 17 & 2 \\ \end{array}\right]& R_3 &:= R_3 +(-8) R_2\\[5pt] &\sim \left[\begin{array}{ccc|c} 1 & -3 & 0 & 1 \\ 0& 1 & 2 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & -6 \\ \end{array}\right]&R_2 &:= R_2 + (-2)R_3 \\[5pt] &\sim \left[\begin{array}{ccc|c} 1 & -3 & 0 & 1 \\ 0& 1 & 0 & 13 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & -6 \\ \end{array}\right]&R_1&:=R_1 + 3R_2 \\[5pt] &\sim \left[\begin{array}{ccc|c} 1 & 0 & 0 & 40 \\ 0& 1 & 0 & 13 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & -6 \\ \end{array}\right].\\ \end{align*}\]

example.title: Finding the Reduced Row Echelon Form of a 3x3 System That Is Not in Row Echelon Form

question.text: Consider the following system of linear equations: \[ \left\{ \begin{align*} &x + 3y + 2z = -5 \\ &x + 4y + 2z = -2 \\ &-2x - 6y -3z = 8 \\ \end{align*} \right. \] Use the standard Gauss-Jordan method to reduce the augmented matrix $M$ of the system to reduced row echelon form, and then solve the linear system.
question.explanation:
The augmented matrix for this system is

\[ M= \left[ \begin{array}{ccc|c} 1 & 3 & 2 & -5 \\ 1 & 4 & 2 & -2 \\ -2 & -6 & -3 & 8 \\ \end{array} \right]. \]

Transforming $M$ to reduced row echelon form, we have

\[\begin{align*} M&\sim \left[\begin{array}{ccc|c} 1 & 3 & 2 & -5 \\ 1 & 4 & 2 & -2 \\ -2 & -6 & -3 & 8 \\ \end{array}\right] & R_2&:= R_2 - R_1 \\[5pt] &\sim \left[\begin{array}{ccc|c} 1 & 3 & 2 & -5 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & 3 \\ -2 & -6 & -3 & 8 \\ \end{array}\right]& R_3 &:= R_3 + 2R_1\\[5pt] &\sim \left[\begin{array}{ccc|c} 1 & 3 & 2 & -5 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & 3 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & -2 \\ \end{array}\right]& R_1 &:= R_1 + (-2)R_3 \\[5pt] &\sim \left[\begin{array}{ccc|c} 1 & 3 & 0 & -1 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & 3 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & -2 \\ \end{array}\right]& R_1 &:= R_1 + (-3)R_2 \\[5pt] &\sim \left[\begin{array}{ccc|c} 1 & 0 & 0 & -10 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & 3 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & -2 \\ \end{array}\right]. \\ \end{align*}\]

The corresponding system is now \[ \left\{ \begin{align*} & x = -10\\ & y= 3\\ & z = -2. \end{align*} \right. \]

So, we have the solution $x = -10$, $y=3$, and $z = -2.$ Or, in vector form, $\langle -10,3,-2 \rangle.$

question.text: Consider the following system of linear equations: \[ \begin{cases} x + 2y - 3z = 1 \\ -4x - 8y + 12z = -4 \\ 2x + 4y - 6z = 2 \end{cases} \] Use the standard Gauss-Jordan method to reduce the augmented matrix $M$ of the system to reduced row echelon form.
question.explanation:
The augmented matrix for this system is \[ M= \left[ \begin{array}{ccc|c} 1 & 2 & -3 & 1 \\ -4 & -8 & 12 & -4 \\ 2 & 4 & -6 & 2 \\ \end{array} \right]. \]

Transforming $M$ to reduced row echelon form, we have

\[\begin{align*} M&\sim \left[\begin{array}{ccc|c} 1 & 2 & -3 & 1 \\ -4 & -8 & 12 & -4 \\ 2 & 4 & -6 & 2 \\ \end{array}\right] & R_2 &:= R_2 + 4R_1\\[5pt] &\sim \left[\begin{array}{ccc|c} 1 & 2 & -3 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0 \\ 2 & 4 & -6 & 2 \\ \end{array}\right]& R_3 &:= R_3 - 2R_1 \\[5pt] &\sim \left[\begin{array}{ccc|c} 1 & 2 & -3 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0 \\ \end{array}\right]. \end{align*}\]
